guidance: Decision aid only: it shows how one origin server would evaluate these four preconditions under RFC 9110. It does not send the request, follow redirects or show what the method itself would return, and a shared cache may apply additional rules.
method: RFC 9110 evaluates the preconditions in a fixed order and stops at the first failure. If-Match comes first: "*" is true when a current representation exists, otherwise one of the listed entity tags must match the current ETag using strong comparison, which never accepts a weak validator or a W/ tag. If-Unmodified-Since is ignored when If-Match is present, when the field value is not a valid HTTP-date, or when the resource has no Last-Modified date; otherwise the condition is true when the last modification time is earlier than or equal to the field date, and a later modification answers 412. If-None-Match uses weak comparison: "*" is false when a representation exists, and a listed tag matches when its opaque tag equals the current ETag, ignoring any W/ prefix. A false If-None-Match answers 304 Not Modified for GET and HEAD and 412 Precondition Failed for every other method. If-Modified-Since is ignored when If-None-Match is present, when the method is not GET or HEAD, when the date is invalid, or when Last-Modified is unavailable; otherwise the condition is false when the representation is no later than the field date, which answers 304. Dates are read in the IMF-fixdate and asctime forms, checked against the calendar and the named weekday, and compared to the second in UTC; the obsolete RFC 850 two-digit-year form is refused, and Range and If-Range are out of scope. The page models one origin server and one target resource, and it never sends a request.
